objective_for_doctor: A 16-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have lower chest pain, left side of the chest pain, and upper chest pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I have pain in my lower chest and the left side of my chest, and also upper chest pain. It feels like a knife-stroke type pain, and I’ve been getting out of breath with minimal effort—also kind of hard to breathe when I lie flat.

Doctor: I’m going to ask a few quick questions to narrow this down: when did the pain start, and is it constant or coming in sharp episodes?  
Doctor: Also, do you have fever, cough, sweating, fainting, or does taking a deep breath/moving make it worse?

The pain started gradually, not suddenly. It’s not constant—more like sharp episodes/knife-stroke pain (about 2 out of 10). I don’t have fever or cough that I know of, and I haven’t fainted. Taking a deep breath and moving makes it worse, and lying flat also makes my breathing worse.

Doctor: Thanks—given sharp pain worsened by deep breaths and lying flat, I’m concerned about pleuritic pain such as pericarditis or a small pleural issue; do you have recent viral illness, sore throat, or new chest injury/strenuous exercise?  
Doctor: Also, any palpitations, dizziness, leg swelling, or recent long travel/surgery?
Yes, I recently had a viral infection. No sore throat that I’m aware of, and no new chest injury. I haven’t had long travel or surgery, and I don’t have leg swelling.

Doctor: Any recent shortness of breath that’s getting worse, and do you feel the pain improves when you sit up and leans forward versus when you lie back?  
Doctor: Also, have you noticed palpitations or chest pounding, and can you point to whether the pain is worse with pressing on a specific spot on your chest?

My shortness of breath feels worse with minimal effort, and it’s worse when I lie back—sitting up helps a bit. I don’t feel like I’ve had palpitations or chest pounding. The pain is on the upper and left side of my chest, and I can point to it, but pressing on a specific spot makes it hurt more.

Doctor: Given sharp pleuritic pain worse lying flat and somewhat better sitting up, plus recent viral illness and worse with deep breaths, I’m concerned about pericarditis (and less likely pneumonia/PE); can you confirm if the pain improves when you sit forward and do you have any recent fever measured, nausea, or recent strenuous exercise?  
Doctor: I’d like to check your vitals and heart/lung exam—REQUEST TEST: ECG and REQUEST TEST: Troponin, plus REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

It does feel a little better when I sit forward, yes. I don’t know of any measured fever, and I haven’t had nausea or recent strenuous exercise. Please go ahead with the ECG, troponin, and chest X-ray.

Doctor: I’m going to review your ECG, troponin, and chest X-ray results next—REQUEST TEST: ECG, REQUEST TEST: Troponin, REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.  
Doctor: While those are pending, can you tell me if you’ve had any recent worsening with coughing, and whether you’ve noticed relief with NSAIDs like ibuprofen?
I haven’t had a worsening cough. I haven’t tried ibuprofen or other NSAIDs yet, so I can’t say if it helped.

Doctor: Based on your symptoms—sharp pleuritic chest pain after a viral illness, worse lying flat and better sitting forward, and worse with deep breaths—I suspect pericarditis; we still need the test results. Have you received/seen the ECG, troponin, and chest X‑ray results yet?  
Doctor: Also, I’ll ask one more: on a 0–10 scale, how severe is the pain now, and does it get better with ibuprofen when you take it (or would you be able to try it if no contraindications)?
I haven’t seen the results yet for the ECG, troponin, or chest X-ray. Right now the pain is about 2 out of 10, and I haven’t taken ibuprofen yet—but I’d be able to try it if you think it’s safe.

Doctor: I’ll request one more set of key tests to rule out heart strain and other causes—REQUEST TEST: Repeat_Vitals_with_O2_sat and REQUEST TEST: CRP/ESR.  
Doctor: If your ECG/troponin are negative and inflammatory markers are elevated, I’m comfortable treating presumptive acute pericarditis—can you take ibuprofen now (if no kidney disease/ulcer/bleeding history) and confirm whether you can?  
Doctor: I’m going to wait for the ECG, troponin, chest X‑ray, and CRP/ESR—then I’ll finalize the diagnosis.

Yes, I can take ibuprofen. I don’t have any known kidney disease, stomach ulcers, or bleeding problems, so it should be safe for me. I’m waiting on the ECG, troponin, chest X-ray, and CRP/ESR results too.

Doctor: While we wait for the ECG, troponin, chest X‑ray, and CRP/ESR, I recommend you start ibuprofen now (with food) and avoid strenuous activity; do you also have any new fever, worsening shortness of breath, or faintness right now?  
Doctor: If any of those occur, or if breathing trouble rapidly worsens, you should go to the ER immediately.  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute pericarditis (likely post-viral) — pleuritic, positional chest pain worse lying flat and with deep breaths, improved sitting forward.

1. Pericarditis
